Definition: from G4973; to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication, to keep secret, to attest:--(set a, set to) seal up, stop.
BiblicalUsage: To seal is to mark as God's and to shut fast. God hath sealed us and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts, believers are sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise, the man who receives Christ's testimony sets to his seal that God is true, and the chief priests seal the stone of the tomb and set a watch.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sealing of the Spirit is God's mark on His people, and no seal of men could hold the tomb shut. I hold that the earnest of the Spirit in my heart is the down payment of all He has promised.
